answer.says: You are quite right. I am obstructing the system of needs. I shall purchase the papers and vanish.
answer.thought: The shopkeeper’s impatience is the logic of the market asserting itself against my idle contemplation. I am a hindrance to the flow of commerce, and as such, I must remove myself. I have forty-six rupees; the newspaper costs forty-five. I can afford the information, but not the luxury of lingering. I will buy the paper and leave, as the universal form of the shopkeeper demands.
